correctness.rationale: An exact normality argument uses total unimodularity of the signed bipartite vertex-edge incidence matrix. Every facet is found by enumerating the 924 affine six-subsets. Intersections give all 349 faces. The checker tests each primitive-normal cone for simpliciality and intrinsic lattice index; all nonsmooth cones are nonsimplicial, and maximal singular faces are exactly eight vertex-star triangles and six antipodal-edge segments. Their orbit closures are coordinate linear planes and lines. An exact Stanley–Reisner face census gives the Hilbert function, polynomial and rational series. The package contains a runnable complete finite verification of the nonstandard facet/cone census; no floating point, random testing, or extrapolation is used. The statement is for the reduced support, not the Jacobian scheme.

value.rationale: The sixfold is attached to two standard natural objects, the hypercube Q3 and the 4-by-4 crown graph. The complete reduced singular support unexpectedly has maximal components of two distinct dimensions: eight P² and six P¹, so this is not just a nonsmoothness witness. The exact incidence pattern and Hilbert series provide a concrete intrinsic and embedding-sensitive geometric classification, beyond smoothness and ambient Hilbert data; nonpurity makes it a useful toric test case. The result excludes nonreduced singular schemes and makes no unsupported extension beyond this object.
